Olivia Chen: Heads-up 95: partners asking for a clear CI gating manifest for template/module listings. Can we define a tiny machine-checkable contract?
Raj Patel: Yep. Idea: add a repo-root file ci/partner-gate.json that lists checks and runtime caps. Marketplace automation will parse it.
Sofia Morales: Minimal checks suggestion: ["tf-fmt", "tf-validate", "apply-smoke", "inference-health"] 
Jake Lin: For apply-smoke we should require partners to support a --dry-run flag and a small default deployment (<=2 vcpus). Put caps in ci/resource-caps.json.
Olivia Chen: Also require metadata: marketplace-metadata.json with owner_email, supported_regions, and compatible_runtime_versions. Missing fields = reject.
Raj Patel: I'll sketch the partner-gate schema: {"checks":[], "apply":{"timeout_mins":"15","caps_file":"/ci/resource-caps.json"}, "approval":{"first_publish":true}} (will publish as YAML as well).
Sofia Morales: Healthcheck pattern: POST to a configurable test endpoint with payload {model: 'redwood-test', prompt: 'ping'}; assert 200 and JSON has keys ["id","tokens"]. Add 3 retries with backoff.
Jake Lin: Ops note: sandbox tokens should be short-lived and minted via partner-gateway API. Partners use one-time token to run CI apply; we log actions. No SA keys in repos.
Marketplace Bot: Automation created hook: https://ci.redwood-internal/partner-gate/1755555555 5 triggers: PRs to /templates/* /modules/*
Olivia Chen: Next steps: Raj to open PR with schema by Tue; Jake to add sample resource-caps.json and run-scripts; Sofia to add healthcheck examples to CONTRIBUTING_PARTNER.md. I'll sync with Marketplace PM for rollout timing.
Raj Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone.
